findings.text: The first paragraph answers what Athena is, who it is for and what problem it solves, in plain words. A newcomer can say what this is within seconds.
findings.source: "Athena is an open-source system, written in Rust, that turns a short request into a change to a code repository. ... It solves the problem of AI edits that arrive unreviewed and unaccountable."

findings.text: The page title and heading are about firstmate, not Athena. A newcomer arriving at Athena's home URL may think they reached the wrong page until they read the second paragraph, which explains that the study is a demonstration.
findings.source: <title>Athena explains how firstmate handles work</title> / h1 of the same text

findings.text: The one section that would show Athena's selling points (models, verdict, cost) shows an error message instead, near the top of the page. This weakens the page's main claim and looks broken to a first-time visitor.
findings.source: Check it on a real job: "The records of job 20261029-073603-7kqv could not be read here, so no models, verdict or costs are shown: no reading record for job 20261029-073603-7kqv."

findings.text: What to do next is concrete and complete: prerequisites, clone, install and a first command, plus a note on which repository it acts on. The page also links to this section from the header.
findings.source: Next steps: "Before installing, check that you have these prerequisites ... Install Athena from the checkout: ./setup.sh ... Try it with a one-line request: athena ask "add a changelog""

findings.text: This header link is meant for the project owner, yet it sits in the newcomer's first screen with no explanation. It is likely to confuse a visitor.
findings.source: "Owner view: proposals waiting for your decision."

findings.text: Almost all of the page is detailed firstmate internals: exit codes, pending-close records, places-held. A newcomer who came to learn about Athena must scroll past it, and the page never says they can skip it.
findings.source: Sections "States of a piece of work", "Why it is built this way", "Glossary", "Claims and sources" (45 claims)

findings.text: Several glossary entries say the term is undefined. This is honest about the sources, but it leaves a newcomer without working definitions for words the page uses.
findings.source: Glossary: "The firstmate source does not define a captain call." / "does not define a durable record" / "does not define an endpoint" / "does not define a heartbeat" / "does not define a wake"

findings.text: The opening paragraph mentions "the verdict" and the checking model but does not explain them. It also does not say what using Athena needs beyond Claude Code, such as an account or what each run costs.
findings.source: "get back a commit they can trace to the request, the models, the cost and the verdict"

findings.text: This section and the footer describe how the page is built inside the repository. That is useful to maintainers but means little to a first-time visitor.
findings.source: About this page: "the name of the folder under studies/ that holds the data this page is generated from"
